explanations.explanation: That's the charge. Amaziah sends word to Jeroboam, "Amos has conspired against you in the midst of the house of Israel." Amaziah is the priest of Bethel, and Jeroboam is Israel's king. He sent word to the king, and I think that tells you a lot.
Nope, no stealing in this message. Amaziah says, "Amos has conspired against you in the midst of the house of Israel." Nobody counts the offering plate here. The charge is about the king.

The Sabbath never comes up in this passage, friend. Amaziah tells the king, "Amos has conspired against you in the midst of the house of Israel." That's the accusation, plain and simple. A conspiracy charge is a big one to send to a king.

Right. Amaziah reports that Amos said, "Jeroboam will die by the sword…" That's Amaziah's report of the words, and I'll tell you, it's not the kind of news a king wants delivered by messenger. Amaziah also says it's why the land can't bear Amos's words.
Old age would've been a much nicer message, baker. But Amaziah reports that Amos said, "Jeroboam will die by the sword…" No rocking chair in that report. That's the message Amaziah sent to the king.
No sickbed in this one. Amaziah reports that Amos said, "Jeroboam will die by the sword…" A sword is a whole different kind of news than a cough. And Amaziah is the one passing it along to the king.

That's the word. Amaziah says Amos claimed, "…Israel will surely go into exile, away from their homeland." Exile means being taken out of your own land. Amaziah is the one reporting it, so these are the words as he tells them to the king.

Battle is close to the sword talk, but it's not the word here. Amaziah reports, "…Israel will surely go into exile, away from their homeland." The key piece is the homeland part. The people are going away from it.

Hiding sounds like a good plan, but it isn't in the report. Amaziah says Amos claimed, "…Israel will surely go into exile, away from their homeland." Exile isn't ducking behind a rock, friend. It's being sent away from home.
Yes, Judah. Amaziah says, "Flee to the land of Judah; earn your bread there and do your prophesying there." Judah is where Amaziah wants Amos to go. He's very sure about the travel plans.
Egypt is a long trip, and Amaziah never mentions it. He tells Amos, "Flee to the land of Judah…" That's the destination he picked. Amaziah named Judah and nothing else.

Moab isn't on his list, baker. Amaziah says, "Flee to the land of Judah; earn your bread there and do your prophesying there." Judah is the place he names. He's pointing Amos away from Bethel in one clear direction.
That's his reason. Amaziah says, "…because it is the sanctuary of the king and the temple of the kingdom." Bethel is what he's talking about. Amos is told to take his prophesying somewhere else.

explanations.answer: It is a city of refuge
explanations.explanation: A city of refuge is a real thing in the Bible, but Amaziah doesn't say that here. His reason is, "…it is the sanctuary of the king and the temple of the kingdom." The word king is right in the sentence.
No school at Bethel in this passage, friend. Amaziah says, "…it is the sanctuary of the king and the temple of the kingdom." That's the reason he gives. It's all about the king.

Not quite. Amos says the opposite: "I was not a prophet…" he says, "nor was I the son of a prophet; rather, I was a herdsman and a tender of sycamore-fig trees." Prophet wasn't his old job, baker. He had a whole different one first.
Yes, False. Amos says, "I was not a prophet…" and adds that he wasn't the son of a prophet either. He was "…a herdsman and a tender of sycamore-fig trees." He tells Amaziah where he really came from.

It was the LORD. Amos says, "But the LORD took me from following the flock and said to me, ‘Go, prophesy to My people Israel.’" Amos wasn't sent by a king or a priest. His answer to Amaziah is all about who sent him.

Uzziah, king of Judah (Amos 1:1), is a real king, but Amos never names him here. He says, "But the LORD took me from following the flock and said to me, ‘Go, prophesy to My people Israel.’" The LORD did the sending.

Hezekiah, a king of Judah (Isaiah 1:1), doesn't show up in this passage at all. Amos says, "But the LORD took me from following the flock and said to me, ‘Go, prophesy to My people Israel.’" The one who took him and sent him is the LORD.
Not this time, baker. Amos says, "You say: ‘Do not prophesy against Israel; do not preach against the house of Isaac.’" He's speaking to Amaziah. The word is for the man who told him to leave.

Right, it's False. Amos says, "Now, therefore, hear the word of the LORD. You say: 'Do not prophesy against Israel…'" The "you" is Amaziah, and the word that follows is for him. Jeroboam isn't the one being spoken to.
Divided is the word. The LORD says to Amaziah, "Your land will be divided by a measuring line…" A measuring line is for marking out portions of land. That's what the LORD says about Amaziah's land.
Sold is a nice, calm guess, but it's not in the text. The LORD says, "Your land will be divided by a measuring line…" The word is divided. Nobody is haggling over the price.
Guarded would be a relief, friend, but that's not the word. The LORD says, "Your land will be divided by a measuring line…" It's divided. That line is a measuring tool, not a security system.
True. The LORD says to Amaziah, "…and you yourself will die on pagan soil." It's part of the word Amos delivers in 7:17. The priest who told Amos to go away hears about his own end.

This one is True, baker. The LORD says, "…and you yourself will die on pagan soil." He's speaking about Amaziah himself, not only his family and land. It's a heavy line, and the text gives it straight.
